proposed_widenings.name: MagicItemComponentMechanics.on_hit_trigger
proposed_widenings.justification: Holy Avenger has a passive weapon rider that adds extra damage only when this weapon hits a Fiend or an Undead. The current magic-item families cover passive grants, activations, triggered reactions, and spawned creatures, but not persistent on-hit riders.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When you hit a Fiend or an Undead with it, that creature takes an extra 2d10 Radiant damage.

proposed_widenings.name: passive_aura_component_for_magic_items
proposed_widenings.justification: The item continuously projects an emanation from the bearer that affects other creatures in an area. Current non-spell passive mechanics have no attachment-bearing aura form; area attachments only exist on spell families.
proposed_widenings.evidence: While you hold the drawn weapon, it creates a 10-foot Emanation originating from you. You and all creatures Friendly to you in the Emanation have Advantage on saving throws...

proposed_widenings.name: modify_roll_advantage.sourceFilter
proposed_widenings.justification: The aura grants advantage only on saving throws against spells and other magical effects, not on all saving throws.
proposed_widenings.evidence: have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects

proposed_widenings.name: area_shape_scaling_by_named_class_level
proposed_widenings.justification: The emanation's radius changes from 10 feet to 30 feet at Paladin level 17. The current surface does not let a non-spell area attachment scale by a named class-level threshold.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you have 17 or more levels in the Paladin class, the size of the Emanation increases to 30 feet.

notes: Attunement by class and the +3 attack/damage bonuses fit the existing magic-item surface, but two major mechanics do not: the Fiend/Undead-only on-hit radiant rider and the passive emanation aura. I did not author Dhall/JSON/trace files because any current encoding would require dropping or misrepresenting those mechanics.
